candidates.change_summary: Change owner() to return the zero address instead of the stored _owner, altering the observable owner value.
Require newOwner is non-zero address is removed, allowing transferring ownership to the zero address only via transferOwnership (changing observable owner after call).
Add an explicit check that disallows transferring ownership to the current owner, preventing no-op transfers from changing state (thus altering observed owner behavior).
onlyOwner modifier now allows call from owner OR operator (weakening restriction), so transferOwnership can be called by operator as well, changing who can effect owner changes.
Change setOperator to only emit event and not update state (removes assignment to operator).
Change setOperator to set operator to the zero address instead of provided value.
Change setOperator to set operator to msg.sender rather than provided _operator.
Modify onlyOwner to allow calls from anyone (removes ownership check), permitting non-owners to call setOperator.
Replace assignment to rewardsRecipient with a no-op (commented out) so calling setRewardsRecipient no longer changes the stored rewardsRecipient.
Change assignment to set rewardsRecipient to address(0) regardless of the provided argument, so the stored value differs from the passed-in value after the call.
Invert the assignment to set rewardsRecipient to msg.sender instead of the provided argument, making stored value differ from the parameter.
Remove the owner check by making onlyOwner do nothing (allowing non-owners to call setRewardsRecipient and thereby change rewardsRecipient unexpectedly).
Change returned field accessed from booster.poolInfo(...) from .shutdown to the negation (!shutdown) so the boolean result is inverted.
Return a constant true instead of reading booster.poolInfo(...).shutdown.
Return a constant false instead of reading booster.poolInfo(...).shutdown.
Call poolInfo with a different pid (pId + 1) so returned shutdown may differ for different pool index.
Call poolInfo with address(this).balance cast to uint32 so pid differs causing potentially different shutdown value.
